headline: The August USDA reports and the European drought landed in the same six-day window: US all-wheat production fell to 1.531 billion bushels, the smallest in decades, while relentless heat cut the French maize crop to 9 million tonnes on the agriculture ministry's own forecast and to under 7 million - the smallest since 1976 - on Expana's and Argus's.
key_points: A BIG WEEK, AND THE SIZE IS REAL RATHER THAN AN ARTEFACT. 45 rows against 6 last week and 88 across five runs on 2026-08-09. The window was six days, shorter than a normal week, but it happened to contain the August WASDE and Crop Production (12 August), the USDA NASS Crop Progress report (10 August), the AHDB second harvest report (14 August), the Environment Agency's weekly drought report (14 August), the JRC/Copernicus drought and wildfire update (12 August) and the Reuters EU maize survey (14 August). Six of the corpus's most productive sources published inside six days.

THE EU MAIZE CROP IS THE STORY, AND THREE FORECASTS DISAGREE BY 3 MILLION TONNES ON FRANCE ALONE. USDA FAS carried France at 10.0 Mt on 10 July (p001, already in the corpus); the French agriculture ministry now says 9.0 Mt, down 35% year on year (s035); Expana and Argus both say under 7 Mt, which would be the smallest since 1976 (s036). All three are recorded. USDA cut EU maize to 50.2 Mt and raised EU imports 1 Mt to 23.5 Mt (s027). Germany's DRV forecasts 4.24 Mt, down 14% (s037). Poland, at about 9 Mt, could become the EU's largest maize producer this year (s038) - the clearest positive row of the week.

UK HARVEST 2026 IS NOW CONFIRMED AS A BAD ONE FOR EVERYTHING EXCEPT OILSEED RAPE. AHDB's second report puts spring barley at 4.1 t/ha with 54% cut, on course for the lowest since records began in 1999, and oats at 4.2 t/ha heading for a 46-year low. Wheat is 6.7 t/ha with 85% cut, down from 6.8 at week 3. Oilseed rape holds at 3.9 t/ha, 18% above the five-year average. AHDB's Helen Plant attributes the shortfall directly to rainfall being in short supply since spring.

ENGLAND'S DROUGHT DEEPENED AGAIN AND IS NOW MEASURABLY BITING FARM WATER SUPPLY. Reservoir storage fell to 65.9% on 11 August, down 3.1 points in a week and 13.8% below the long-term average; 71% of England by land area is in drought with no area at normal status; abstraction restrictions rose to 1,544. Section 57 statutory cuts now bind 288 spray irrigation licences in East Anglia to 31 October, with 14 Wensum-catchment abstractors ordered to cease abstraction entirely. The agency reports crops being lost outright and boreholes drying up.

THE US PICTURE IS SPLIT, NOT UNIFORMLY BAD, AND THE SPLIT IS GEOGRAPHIC. Corn production rose to 16.013 bb and soybeans to a record 4.519 bb on 1.4 million extra planted acres each, but the corn yield was cut 2.3 bu/acre to 180.7 and wheat fell to its smallest in decades. State conditions show the divide: Iowa corn 78% good-to-excellent against Kansas 47%, and North Dakota soybeans at 31% against Iowa's 77%. Kansas winter wheat production is down 44.8% year on year.

what_changed: Last week's summary covered a one-day window and six rows, all from the Environment Agency. This week is the opposite: a six-day window that happened to catch the August USDA cycle, the AHDB harvest report and the JRC drought update together. What actually moved: England's reservoir storage fell from 69% to 65.9% and abstraction restrictions from 1,534 to 1,544, so both those series now have three and four readings respectively and still no label. The agency also revised its own Section 57 figure down from 302 affected abstractors to 288, and revised August rainfall to date up from 4% to 6% of average - the second self-revision from this source in two weeks, recorded rather than absorbed. On the UK harvest, wheat slipped from 6.8 to 6.7 t/ha, spring barley from 5.3 to 4.1 and oats from 4.9 to 4.2 as the combines moved north, which is the opposite of what AHDB had hoped for and it says so explicitly. Winter barley at 6.8 t/ha and oilseed rape at 3.9 t/ha were unchanged and merged as corroboration rather than inserting. New this week and absent from every prior summary: the EU maize collapse now has three competing France forecasts in the corpus, and Lamb Weston has become the first company this season to flag European potato heat damage as a price risk on the record.

conflicts.note: THREE FORECASTS FOR THE 2026 FRENCH MAIZE CROP, NOT RESOLVED. p001 (USDA FAS, published 2026-07-10) says 10.0 million tonnes. s035 (French agriculture ministry, via Reuters, published 2026-08-14) says 9.0 million tonnes, down 35% on 2025. s036 (Expana and Argus, same Reuters wire) says under 7 million tonnes, which would be the smallest since 1976. The spread is 3+ million tonnes on one crop in one country five weeks apart, and it is a genuine disagreement about how much of the crop irrigation will salvage and how much will be chopped for fodder rather than harvested for grain. s036 is recorded unquantified on purpose: 'less than 7 million tons' is an upper bound and converting it to a point value would be inferring a number.

THE ENVIRONMENT AGENCY REVISED ITS OWN SECTION 57 FIGURE AND BOTH READINGS STAND. r005 (published 2026-08-07) says 302 abstractors served notices in East Anglia. s012 (published 2026-08-14) says 288 spray licences, with the restriction running 10 August to 31 October and 14 Wensum-catchment abstractors required to cease entirely. Same agency, same measure, one week apart. Recorded as a revision, not corrected. s012 carries a review_flag naming r005.

SECOND SELF-REVISION FROM THE SAME SOURCE, ON AUGUST RAINFALL. r004 (published 2026-08-07) put England's August rainfall to date at 4% of the long-term average. s010 (published 2026-08-14) puts it at 6%, on 4mm received. Both sit in GB|england|mixed_grains|rainfall_pct_normal|Environment Agency, which now holds four readings - 7% and 10% for July, 4% and 6% for August - and still has no label, so it remains chartable:false. A human needs to decide whether that chart should show revisions or only final figures.

NOT A CONTRADICTION, A TENSION WORTH NAMING. s019 records US corn production UP to 16.013 bb with hazard_type favourable, because the quote says production increased; s018 records the yield DOWN 2.3 bu/acre to 180.7 with hazard_type heat. Both are true and both come from the same report: 1.4 million extra planted acres more than offset a weather-driven yield loss. A reader looking only at production would miss the weather signal entirely.

SCHEMA/PROVENANCE NOTE, NOT A DISAGREEMENT. s026 (Kansas winter wheat, 191.4 million bushels, -44.8% year on year) is the only row this week whose verbatim_quote is a table row from the NASS Agricultural Statistics Board briefing rather than a prose sentence. The figures are read directly from the Planted/Harvested/Yield/Production columns and the row carries a review_flag saying so. Flagged rather than dropped, because it is the sharpest state-level fall in the report.

GB potato wholesale price, recorded with a caveat. The source says UK wholesale potato prices rose by 'more than 40%', an open-ended lower bound. 40 is recorded as the value and the unit carries the qualifier; the incoming row merged into a005, which already held the same figure from an earlier run. Do not chart without a human check.
